text.p: An independent plan launched on Thursday to build a commercial railway tunnel between Finland's capital Helsinki and Tallinn in Estonia is totally unrealistic, a senior Finnish transport ministry official said.

According to the plan by a group of private individuals, the tunnel would cost eight billion markka ($1.6 billion) and need state guaranteed loans but head of transport infrastructure Juhani Tervala said the state had no intention of backing it.
"The real cost would be double that and the whole process has nothing to do with the real world," Tervala told Reuters by telephone. "It is something between April Fool's and May Day."

He noted that the group, called the Helsinki-Tallinn Rail Tunnel Association, was formed solely by private individuals and said "even people with their feet slightly in the air would not back the project."
Finnish news agency STT said the association expected it would take some 10 years to build the tunnel across the Bay of Finland but Tervala said he did not know who would benefit.

The group argues that the tunnel would boost tourism and Finland's competitiveness, STT said, adding the plan was backed by some 70 professors, leaders of unions, municipalities, regional centres and cities and some Helsinki City officials. ($ = 5.137 Finnish Markka)
